name: K-ETA (Korea Electronic Travel Authorization) / Short-term C-3 visa

requirements.blocker_text: K-ETA is only available to nationals of countries participating in Korea's Visa Waiver Programme (roughly 110+ countries); other nationalities need a Short-term C-3 visa instead.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for a Short-term C-3 visa at a Korean embassy or consulate if not visa-waiver eligible.

requirements.blocker_text: K-ETA and the C-3 visa cover tourism, short business visits, transit, and similar purposes; they do not authorise employment or study.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for the relevant work or study route instead if the purpose is employment or enrolled study.

evidence_required.document: Online K-ETA application, typically approved within 24-72 hours

outcome.duration_length: K-ETA valid 3 years (or until passport expiry) for stays up to 90 days per visit, depending on nationality
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: up to 90 days per visit, exact cap varies by nationality's bilateral visa-waiver agreement

sources.title: K-ETA (Korea Electronic Travel Authorization) -- official Korea Immigration Service portal

notes: K-ETA (launched 2021) is a pre-screening electronic travel authorization layered on top of Korea's existing visa-waiver agreements, not a visa itself -- nationals who need a visa outside the waiver programme still apply for a Short-term C-3 visa through a consulate rather than K-ETA. Change of status to a long-term category (study, work, family) from inside Korea while on K-ETA/C-3 status is generally not permitted; applicants typically need to leave and re-apply for the target visa from outside Korea, mirroring the general pattern seen across most 'visit' category routes in this dataset.
